chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Al-Iman (faith) is that which settles in the heart and leads with it to Allah (Exalted and Majestic), and the deeds ratify it with obedience to Allah and submission to His Command; but Al-Islam (submission) is what is apparent from words or deeds, and it is what the communities of people are upon, from all of the sects. And by it, the bloods are saved, and upon it flow the inheritances, and the marriages are validated, and they gather upon the Salat (prayer), and the Zakat (alms-tax), and the Sawm (fasting), and the Hajj (pilgrimage).'

Thus, by that, they are exiting from the Kufr (disbelief) and entering into the Iman; but the Islam does not include the Iman, but the Iman does include the Islam, and they are both together in the words and the deeds, just as the Ka'bah comes to be in the Masjid, and the Masjid is not in the Ka'bah, similarly the Iman includes the Islam, but the Islam does not include the Iman.'
The Bedouins say: We believe. Say: You do not believe but say, We submit; and Iman (belief) has not yet entered into your hearts.

And the Words of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) are the most truthful of the words. I said, 'So is there a preference for the Mu'min (Believer) upon the Muslim with regards to anything from the merits, and the Ordinances, and the legal punishments, and other than that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No. They both flow with regards to that with one flow, but the Mu'min has superiority upon the Muslim regarding their deeds and (through) which they are getting closer to Allah (Exalted and Majestic).'

I said, 'Isn't Allah (Exalted and Majestic) Saying: Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it, and you alleged they are together upon the Salat, and the Zakat, and the Sawm, and the Hajj along with the Mu'mineen (plural of Mu'min)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hasn't Allah (Exalted and Majestic) Said: Who is it that who will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He will Multiply it to him manifold? So, the Mu'mineen, they are those for whom Allah (Exalted and Majestic) would Multiply their good deeds, for every good deed, a multiple of seventy. Thus, this is the superiority of the Mu'min, and Allah (Exalted and Majestic) will Increase for him with regards to the good deeds, upon a measurement of the health of his Iman, a manifold multiple, and Allah (Exalted and Majestic) Does with the Mu'mineen whatever He (Exalted and Majestic) so Desires to, from the goodness.'

I said, 'What is your view of the one who enters into Al-Islam, would he not have entered into the Iman?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No. But he would have been guided to the Iman and exited from the disbelief, and I shall strike for you an example you can get to know by it the superiority of the Iman over the Islam.'

What is your view, if you were to see a man in the Masjid, would you testify that you have seen him to be in the Ka'bah?' I said, 'That is not allowed for me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So if you were to see a man in the Ka'bah, would you bear witness that he had entered the Sacred Masjid?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And how is that?' I said, 'He could not have arrived to enter the Ka'bah unless he had entered the Masjid (first).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are correct, and have done well.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Like that is the Iman and the Islam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Iman in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) delineates the ontological relationship between Islam (ẓāhir, outward submission) and Iman (bāṭin, inward conviction), establishing that while Islam serves as the legal basis for community unity and rulings, Iman represents the deeper spiritual reality. The Imam employs the precise analogy of the Ka'bah being contained within the Masjid al-Haram to illustrate that Iman encompasses Islam, yet Islam does not fully encompass Iman. This distinction clarifies that while all believers are Muslims, not all Muslims possess the fullness of Iman, a nuance critical to Shia theological understanding of faith and reward.
